questions.question: What type of switch uses specialized hardware to make forwarding decisions?
questions.explanation: Layer 3 switches perform routing functions at wire speed using hardware ASICs.

questions.question: What algorithm do switches use to prevent loops in redundant topologies?
questions.explanation: STP prevents network loops by blocking redundant paths while maintaining backup routes.

questions.question: What type of switching reads only the destination address before forwarding?
questions.explanation: Cut-through switching forwards frames immediately after reading the destination address.

questions.question: What type of switching reads the entire frame before forwarding?
questions.explanation: Store-and-forward reads the entire frame and checks for errors before forwarding.

questions.question: What allows multiple VLANs to traverse a single link?
questions.explanation: Trunk ports carry traffic for multiple VLANs using tagging protocols like 802.1Q.

questions.question: What technique do routers use to reduce routing table size?
questions.explanation: Route summarization combines multiple routes into a single routing table entry.

questions.question: What type of firewall inspects packet contents and tracks connections?
questions.explanation: Stateful firewalls track connection states and inspect packet contents for security.

questions.question: What device combines router, switch, and wireless access point functions?
questions.explanation: Integrated routers combine multiple networking functions in a single device.

questions.question: What IEEE 802.11 amendment enables fast roaming handoff between access points?
questions.explanation: 802.11r (Fast BSS Transition) pre-authenticates devices to neighboring APs, cutting handoff time during roaming.

questions.question: What hardware component in switches makes wire-speed forwarding possible?
questions.explanation: ASICs are specialized chips that perform switching operations at hardware speed.

questions.question: What switching method reads only the first 64 bytes of a frame before forwarding?
questions.explanation: Fragment-free switching checks the first 64 bytes, where most collisions occur, before forwarding.

questions.question: What is the IEEE standard number for the original Spanning Tree Protocol?
questions.explanation: Classic STP is defined by IEEE 802.1D.

questions.question: What Cisco-proprietary first-hop redundancy protocol provides gateway redundancy?
questions.explanation: HSRP creates a virtual gateway IP shared between routers for failover.

questions.question: What faster version of STP is defined by IEEE 802.1w?
questions.explanation: RSTP converges in seconds rather than the 30-50 seconds of classic STP.

questions.question: What Cisco protocol dynamically negotiates trunk links between switches?
questions.explanation: DTP negotiates whether a link becomes a trunk and is often disabled for security.

questions.question: A 24-port switch replaces a hub on a busy Ethernet segment with all ports populated. How many separate collision domains does the switch create?
questions.explanation: Each switch port is its own collision domain, so 24 populated ports create 24 collision domains; a hub creates only one.

questions.question: Frames arrive at a switch destined for a MAC address that is not yet in its address table. What does the switch do with those frames?
questions.answer: floods them out all ports except the incoming port
questions.explanation: A switch floods frames with an unknown destination MAC out every port except the one they arrived on until it learns the address.

questions.question: What table does a switch use to associate learned MAC addresses with their corresponding ports?
questions.explanation: The MAC address table (also called the CAM table or forwarding table) maps source MAC addresses to the ports they were learned on.

questions.question: A router connects three separate LAN segments, one per routed interface. How many broadcast domains exist across this topology?
questions.explanation: Routers do not forward broadcasts, so each routed interface delimits a separate broadcast domain - 3 interfaces means 3 domains.

questions.question: A router receives a packet whose destination matches no route entry and no default route is configured. What does the router do with the packet?
alternatives: drops the packet (and sends an ICMP destination unreachable message)
questions.explanation: With no matching route and no default gateway of last resort, the router drops the packet and typically returns an ICMP destination unreachable message.
